indicators.note: the little dog keeps the support held inside it

parts.note: a pup is a young, little dog

explanation.surface: A small dog has settled down while someone props it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settled' looks like the dog lying down; it is the definition, as in a bill that has been paid up.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from bookkeeping: a settled bill or subscription has had every penny handed over.

indicators.note: the letters of IN TIARA are made over again in a new order

explanation.surface: A writer is once more wearing a tiara.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it places the writer inside the tiara, but it is part of the fodder: IN TIARA has exactly the seven letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone authoritarian is strict, demanding obedience.

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' turns the word to read from bottom to top

parts.note: any girl's name will do; here Emma

explanation.surface: Someone is hushing up a problem involving a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover up' reads as the phrase for concealing something, but it splits into LID and a turnaround instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a problem, specifically a hard choice.

clue.text: Fit for drinking by Italian river board

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
a board is a table, as in 'board and lodging'

explanation.surface: Water from an Italian river, served at a table, is safe to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' just places the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: potable comes from Latin potare, to drink, and describes water safe to drink.

indicators.note: the letters have gone off, gone bad, and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A listing of porters' rooms, for instance, that have been sold off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sold off' reads as one phrase, but 'sold' is fodder with 'eg' and 'off' is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A porter's lodge is the gatehouse room where a college or building porter works.

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Lilac trim has been woven into something.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans the gap between the two words, which is why it hides so well.
explanation.definitionFit: Laced threads are interwoven, like the laces through a shoe.

indicators.note: to flip something is to turn it over, so I'D turns into DI

explanation.surface: Someone would lose their temper, have a drink, and have a good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig in!' is what you say when food is served: start eating and enjoy it.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Dig in!' is an invitation to tuck in and enjoy the meal.

indicators.note: to manipulate is to handle and move around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is learning how to push around some skinny gentlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Learning' looks like part of the action, someone learning to manipulate; it is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of knowledge gained; the Enlightenment was also the 18th-century age of reason.

clue.text: Holding breath let icon physically fit

indicators.note: the words hold the answer inside them

parts.note: the letters run across all three words: the end of the first, all of the second, the start of the third

explanation.surface: An icon of fitness is told to hold his breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding breath' reads as one instruction to the icon, but 'Holding' is the whole mechanism and 'breath' is only a container for letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word comes from the athlete, whose trained body is the model of fitness.

clue.text: Learner in confusion back for a game

indicators.note: the learner goes inside the confusion
the result is then read backwards

parts.note: to be in a fog is to be confused
L = learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A learner, flustered, comes back for another game.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside FOG to make FLOG, and FLOG read backwards is GOLF.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the clue names only the category, and golf is one member of it.

definitions.meaning: a loud, deep bang, like thunder or a big gun
a floating line of logs or a chain stretched across a harbour mouth to keep ships out

explanation.surface: A loud bang comes from the barrier across a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: The harbour boom is a chain or line of floating timbers stretched across the entrance to keep ships out.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a bang and a floating harbour barrier are called a boom.

clue.text: Banter not good to the elderly

parts.note: to = in, as in 'come to' or 'go in' a place
age = the old, as in 'youth and age'

explanation.surface: Teasing talk that is unkind to old people.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a complaint about rude banter aimed at the old; the definition and the wordplay describe the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym borrowed from French: playful, teasing talk, from badiner, to joke.

explanation.surface: The pirate of Treasure Island keeps up a steady pace.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay; Long John Silver is the pirate in Treasure Island.
explanation.definitionFit: Long John Silver is the one-legged pirate of Stevenson's Treasure Island.

clue.text: Obligation to hold record for second-in-command

indicators.note: the obligation holds the record inside it

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: The deputy has a duty to keep the records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' here is the music format, the short extended-play disc, not a written record a deputy might keep.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a deputy stands in for the chief and takes over when they are absent.

clue.text: Dad is in trouble — show contempt

explanation.surface: Dad is in trouble, and someone sneers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' reads as part of 'in trouble', but it is also fodder: DAD IS IN has the seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the verb means to look down on something as unworthy, which is showing contempt.

clue.text: Attach round rickety boat as fuel source

indicators.note: a rickety boat is falling apart, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: to peg is to attach, as washing to a line

explanation.surface: Someone ties a rope round a shaky boat to use it as firewood.
explanation.walkthrough: A peat bog is where peat, a turf burnt as fuel in Ireland and Scotland, is cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Peat is dug from a peat bog and dried to burn, so the bog is a fuel source.

parts.note: OBEs, Officers of the Order of the British Empire, are British honours

explanation.surface: An aristocrat is handed honours in a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: The break falls in a different place from the pieces: EARL + OBES, read as EAR LOBES. An OBE is a British honour given by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ear lobes are parts of the ears of those who listen.

definitions.meaning: lift is the British word for an elevator

explanation.walkthrough: One definition is a verb and the other a noun; lift is the British word for an elevator.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the verb means raises, and the noun is the British word for elevators.

clue.text: Animal is in good French surroundings

indicators.note: 'in' places IS inside the next part, the way a person is in a room

explanation.surface: An animal is living in pleasant French surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue uses two container indicators at once, 'in' and 'surroundings', one for each side of the same step.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the bison, the American buffalo, is one of many animals the clue could mean.

indicators.note: the nut is cracked open and its letters broken up

explanation.surface: A family member is cracking open a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' also means an eccentric, so the surface can be read as a relative who is a bit cracked.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an aunt, a parent's sister, is one kind of relative.

clue.text: Not a serious quarrel but it turns very loud

indicators.note: something that turns ends up facing the other way, so IT is read backwards

parts.note: ff = fortissimo, very loud in music

explanation.surface: A row that is only minor, but it gets very noisy.
explanation.walkthrough: FF is the musical marking fortissimo, very loud.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a small, short-lived squabble is exactly what 'not a serious quarrel' describes.

parts.note: sh! is a call for quiet
to amble is to walk slowly

explanation.surface: Someone strolls silently into a scene of disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' looks like an insertion instruction; here it only joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a shambles was once a meat market or slaughterhouse, and now means a scene of total disorder.

indicators.note: the point goes inside the wedding

parts.note: S = south, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: The key point of a wedding is being together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' reads as the purpose of a wedding, but it is a compass point. Compass points (N, S, E, W) are a common source of single letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In unison means together, in agreement.

parts.note: NE = north-east, the region of England that Tyneside is in
a gate gives access to a garden

explanation.surface: Tynesiders are refused entry to a garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside, around Newcastle, lies in the north-east of England, hence NE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to negate is to rule something untrue, or to cancel its effect.
